current.text: He is projected to come off the bench as the sixth man and the main creator for the bench units. The projected starters are Suggs, Bane, Franz Wagner, Banchero and Wendell Carter Jr.
Yahoo lists him as questionable with an ankle injury.

Orlando will not extend his rookie contract, so he becomes a restricted free agent next offseason. Orlando is close to the second apron and will likely have to choose between keeping Suggs and keeping him.
Phil expects his next contract to be at least 23 million USD per year.
His best numbers last season came when teammates were out. After December he settled in as a 12 to 13 point per game player.

The experts call him overrated. They do not expect him to play 30 minutes and see him as a stash who needs an injury ahead of him. He is probably not worth a draft pick, and only fine around pick 135 if two players ahead of him are hurt.
If Suggs goes down, he should start and be worth rostering.
Orlando has a new head coach, Sean Sweeney. His rotation preferences are unknown, so bench roles may change.

durable.text: He is an inefficient scorer. His FG% and FT% are below average and his 3-point shot is not reliable.
Steals are his best category. He adds few rebounds and assists for his role.
His usage is above 20%, but he does not pass much for a ball handler.
He is a good on-ball defender, but he struggles against screens and is not at Suggs's level defensively.

note: He ranks 147 on Yahoo and 128 on ESPN and is priced at 0 to 1 USD, so he sits at the edge of our 144-player draft. The newest notes say to leave him undrafted: he is a bench sixth man on a 45% FG and 75% FT profile, and steals (about 1.4 per game) are his only real asset. Watch him on waivers early. Check his ankle, his minutes under the new coach, and Suggs's health, since a Suggs injury would make him a starter worth adding.
